text: Version 5 of the Epic 1 BRD is written in Draft status and carries no approval.
why: The sources hold no Product Owner approval for version 4 or for version 5, and this run takes no human approval step.
read: Root AGENTS.md rule 9 and the D-RCV-60 overlay (missing approval is recorded as an assumption and the document stays Draft)
confirm: Product owner approves version 5 at the next requirements review
impact: The document may not be used as an approved baseline until it is signed

text: The business requirement IDs of this epic are the RWB-E1-nnn and RWB-ACE-001 keys used since version 1; they are the BR IDs of section 9 and are not renumbered.
why: The realignment requires stable BR IDs, and the family has always used the RWB-E1-nnn keys.
read: BRD v4 section 3; D-RCV-60 realignment instruction 'BR IDs stable'
impact: No cross-reference in the story set changes

text: Every release date is copied from version 4 and marked (tentative); no date is changed.
why: Template and Rules U7 and DL48 fix the dates as tentative and unchanged.
read: Template and Rules section R1 (U7) and section R8.1
impact: No date is raised as a gap

text: The primary service epic of a requirement is the 'primary' chapter of the requirement in the split plan, read against the Ownership Map v1 service sheet.
why: The BRD carries module headings only, so the service that delivers a key has to come from the ownership source.
read: split_plan.json legacy entries; Ownership Map v1 Services sheet
impact: A key whose primary changes moves in one row of section 9 only

text: A key whose primary chapter is PLT maps to the single platform epic of its story slices: RWB-E1-044 to RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-E1-047 to RWB-PLT-LIB and RWB-E1-056 to RWB-PLT-OBS.
why: Three Epic 1 requirements are platform work and the split plan names the platform epic only inside the story slices.

text: The story count in section 9 is the number of story slices the plan holds for the key, not a business quantity.
why: The BRD is a business document; the count is given only to show that one requirement is delivered by several stories.
impact: The count changes if the story set changes; no business statement depends on it

text: The decision-owner labels in section 7 are copied unchanged from version 4; they are decision handles, not names, and no person is named or added.
why: Section 7 is business content of the source and must stay word for word.
read: BRD v4 section 7; Root AGENTS.md rule 4
confirm: Business owner replaces the handles with role names at the next review

text: The requirement text of RWB-E1-014, RWB-E1-029 and RWB-E1-048 is unchanged; their realignment position appears only in section 8.5, section 9 and the gap register.
why: Version 5 changes delivery, not business content, and the three positions are decisions for the business owner.
read: D-RCV-60 realignment instruction 'business content unchanged'; Template and Rules section R6
confirm: Product owner confirms the three positions
impact: Three live requirements have no story in this wave

text: The section 3 headings keep the module names of version 4 (for example 'P1 Recovery data engine'), while section 8.1 uses the Ownership Map v1 service name (rwb-source-data, Source data).
why: Renumbering or renaming the headings would break the section references and the keys of the source document.
read: BRD v4 section 3 headings; Ownership Map v1 Services sheet
impact: The two naming styles sit side by side in version 5

text: The wave in section 9 is the business-epic wave of Template and Rules R5.6 (EP01 is wave 1), even where the service's Architecture v5 wave is later.
why: R5.6 keeps the earlier wave and records one conflict per service and business epic.
read: Template and Rules section R5.6; Ownership Map v1 Services sheet
confirm: Delivery lead confirms at build sequencing
impact: Three services build three Epic 1 story groups earlier than their own wave

text: Version 5 is dated 22 November 2026 and version 4 keeps its date of 15 November 2026 in the change-log table.
why: The change log has to show both versions, and the new version needs its own date.
read: Template and Rules section R8.1 and section R8.2
applied_in: Document control table and change log

text: The four decision-owner cells of section 7 that named people (DL06, DL09, DL12 and DL20) carry the Template and Rules section R9 placeholder; the owner role is not stated in the source.
why: Root AGENTS.md rule 4 forbids names of people anywhere, and the source gives a person handle instead of a role.
read: Root AGENTS.md rule 4; Template and Rules section R9 placeholder
applied_in: Section 7 rows DL06, DL09, DL12 and DL20
confirm: Business lead states the four owner roles
impact: The four decisions show no named owner until the role is stated
